answer: SybilRank short-random-walk scoring resists sybils: trust is the landing probability of short random walks launched from the honest seed, and walks rarely cross the sparse cut into a sybil region. A voyage of fakes behind a thin set of attack edges receives vanishingly few walk-landings — the knoll of honest mass keeps the walks local to the honest side. A juniper-dense internal sybil graph cannot attract walks that start honest and stay short; the ranking a fake earns is bounded by how often a brief honest-origin walk leaks across the limited attack edges, which stays tiny.
